Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives buttery-smooth motion at a sustainable TDP; FSR at a mild render scale keeps the image sharp enough while relieving GPU pressure. This is the recommended daily-driver profile for planetary exploration and space flight.

profiles.Summary: No Man's Sky runs well on the Steam Deck as a Verified title, with the RDNA 2 GPU sitting just at the minimum spec tier, making medium settings with upscaling the sweet spot for a stable experience. The procedurally generated open-world nature of the game means performance can vary significantly between space, planetary surfaces, and dense base areas.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1060 / RX 470 minimum, which the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU sits just below) and the Deck's hardware capabilities. On first run, check frame rate during planetary landing and in any player base — those are the heaviest scenarios — and dial settings down if frame rate dips below your cap.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at sub-native resolution with FSR upscaling and a low TDP cap gives the longest session life; 30 fps feels stable for this exploration-paced game. Drop texture quality to Low if battery life is still insufficient.

KnownIssues: Performance can drop noticeably in large, player-built bases or busy multiplayer hubs
Shader compilation stutters may occur on first visit to new biome types
Some UI text can appear small at 1280x800 native resolution
Occasional graphical glitches or crashes reported under certain Proton versions — Proton Experimental is generally recommended

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapped at full TDP can reach 60 fps in space and on sparse planets, but expect dips to 45 fps in lush biomes or near large bases; FSR at 1152x720 keeps the image acceptable while giving the GPU headroom. Battery life is short — keep a charger handy for long sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh lock paired with a 40 fps cap delivers a smooth, judder-free experience that suits No Man's Sky's exploration pace well. FSR at 1024x640 recovers enough GPU headroom to hold the cap through most planetary surfaces.

profiles.Summary: No Man's Sky runs well on the Steam Deck OLED with its native Linux support and full controller integration, though its procedurally generated open worlds and demanding visuals mean the RDNA 2 GPU needs careful tuning to stay smooth. With FSR upscaling and reduced settings, a stable 40–60 fps is achievable depending on the scene complexity.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1060 / RX 470 class, which is modestly above the Deck's GPU), the game's Verified status, and ProtonDB's gold/trending-platinum tier. On first run, check frame pacing during a planetary landing — that is the hardest moment for the hardware — and step down to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if the frame rate dips below your cap consistently.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU load low enough for extended sessions; expect occasional dips during planetary landings even at these settings. GPU clock is manually capped to reduce power draw further.

KnownIssues: Planetary landings and large base areas can cause significant frame dips due to procedural generation load spikes
Multiplayer sessions with multiple players on-screen increase GPU and CPU load noticeably
Some shader compilation stutters may occur on first visits to new biomes or systems
Occasional audio crackle or desync reported under Proton, though generally minor

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full TDP and native resolution the Deck can push 60 fps in space stations and low-complexity planets, but dense biomes and bases will pull it back to the mid-40s — consider dropping the cap to 45 if stutter is noticeable. Battery life is short at this setting, so keep a charger handy.
